Messages.Author: Martin
Messages.Body:


We played for the first time in the prophecies a week and a half ago, we
hadn't received the prophecies so some friendly guy from WW had mailed
our local prince two of them. There was general agreement among the
players I talked to, that the rules made the games more interesting. And
I didn't hear anybody say they destroyed the game in any way.

Personally I think that it is a great initiative from WW, and well worth
the money. Currently players are speculating on what rule will be used
again, and how to make decks that takes it into account. I see it in
this way - either you can make a deck that uses the extra rule to make
something nasty/funny/new/etc, OR you make a deck that works well
against the kinds of decks you *think* will be played because of the rule ;)

All in all a big thumbs up to the designers of the prophecies league,
keep up the good work.

Martin aka. the frickin moron

- Waiting in anticipation to see the next envelope opened

>this way - either you can make a deck that uses the extra rule to make
>something nasty/funny/new/etc, OR you make a deck that works well

The last - building decks that work against the decks you think will be built -
seems like the really cool thing about the rules. A player pointed out an
incredibly amusing hoser for what could be expected, but I had already built my
decks for last session.

Unfortunately, I don't think our league's players are caring much in general
what the rules are and mostly just seeing what random things start happening
using their normal decks. So, we lack any sort of feature of metagame
analysis.
